payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 3, Attributes (quarto-book/chapters/03-attributes.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the
Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook. The source registered in this run IS the chapter file;
its label is `03-attributes`. Cite findings as `03-attributes.qmd:LINE`.

## Disposition plan format (librarian, final synthesis)
Classify every finding into exactly one tier:
- **mechanical**: chapter-local, zero mechanics change, no content judgment (heading
  levels, table rows, wording, captions, cross-refs, stale vocabulary, math typos,
  pagebreaks, em-dashes).
- **substantive**: new content, multi-file, or cross-chapter reconciliation.
- **design-decision**: touches budget/prereqs/new rules/canon/balance; needs Bruce's veto.

## Locked conventions (the law)
- One-roll principle: the 3d6 attack/casting/check roll IS the outcome roll. No damage
  dice, no second roll. Tiers: Weak 1-8, Standard 9-14, Strong 15-18+ (ch06).
- Damage budget (flat, not dice): Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21. No flat
  +N damage riders anywhere (the riders-die law; "+1 damage tier" is the only bump).
- Card costs flat 2/4/8 DP. Prereq shapes: Adept = exactly 2 ranks, Master = exactly 3.
  Level gates: Adept L3, Master L7.
- Zero em-dashes in book text. No dice in damage/healing.
- Condition vocabulary is leveled (Burning X, Poisoned X, Slowed X, Frozen X).
  Bespoke phrasing that duplicates a condition is a residual to convert.
- Melee attack = 3d6 + Brawn; Finesse weapons use Agility. Melee attacks ADD your
  Brawn (or Agility if Finesse) to the damage row. Missiles/thrown are flat, no
  attribute added. (ch06, ch13, ch15)
- Skills key to attributes (ch07 roster, 22 skills): Athletics/Brawn, Acrobatics/Agility,
  History/Knowledge, Religion/Knowledge, Persuasion/Guile, Deception/Guile,
  Intimidation/Brawn, Thievery/Agility, Sleight of Hand/Agility.
- Divine spells roll 3d6 + Reason + relevant skill; arcane spells roll 3d6 + Knowledge
  + relevant skill (ch10).
- Attribute canon: scores -2..+2, spread totals exactly +3, increases at levels 4 and 8
  (ch18). Starting HP = 10 + Fortitude + Knowledge; +Fortitude (min 1) per level after
  L1. Initiative = 3d6 + Agility. Carry slots = 10 + (Brawn x 5). (ch02 Table 2.3, ch21)
- Dwarf ancestry gift Sturdy = +2 maximum HP (ch04).
- Canon party (ch13 worked examples): Kael = dwarf Blade, Brawn +1, Agility +2;
  Roric = dwarf Protector, Brawn +2; Lyra = halfling Odd; Ser Aldric = party Leader,
  Guile +1 (ch14:96 uses Guile +1 + Persuasion Adept +2).

## Verified context (recon already done; trust this, but re-verify any claim you
plan to act on against the chapter text itself)
- The chapter is 164 lines, 7 sections, 6 worked examples, 0 em-dashes, 0 damage dice.
- Intimidation is keyed to BRAWN in ch07:139 and ch22:175 (added to the roster 2026-08-27,
  decision #29), but the chapter's Guile description may still claim Guile covers
  intimidation. ch03 predates the Intimidation addition.
- ch03:64 dwarf HP example: 10 + FO 2 + KN 0 + Sturdy 2 = 14. Sturdy is real (ch04:45).
  Verify the arithmetic and the wording.
- ch03:158-162 Zara example: "Zara, the Unbalanced" (canon per PR #394, decision #74),
  rolls "3d6 + Reason (+2) + Religion Novice (+1)". Religion is keyed to Knowledge in
  ch07, BUT divine spells roll 3d6 + Reason + relevant skill per ch10. Decide whether
  the example reads as a divine spell roll (compliant) or a skill check (wrong attribute).
- ch03:120 "The Poisoned condition kicks in, Bane on all attacks" vs ch13's leveled
  condition "Poisoned X: takes X poison damage per round and attacks at Bane".

## Your job
Each member: audit through your lens, file findings with severity (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW),
exact file:line, what is wrong, and the concrete fix. Report findings as JSON per the
packet schema. Do not invent problems; verify against the chapter text before claiming.
The librarian synthesizes the disposition plan (tiered, atomicity noted where fixes
interlock) and writes the final recommendation.

payload.argument: Verified the chapter against the locked conventions as a publishable unit: the six worked examples all sum correctly (five land 15 Strong, one lands 10 Standard), the attribute spread totals +3, the dwarf starting-HP example computes 10 + 2 + 0 + 2 = 14 including the Sturdy bonus, and there are no em-dashes or damage dice. The chapter does not hold as written, though, because two passages still carry stale cross-chapter canon. First, the Guile description at 03-attributes.qmd:82 lists intimidation among what Guile governs, but the current skill roster (07-skills.qmd:139) keys Intimidation to Brawn; the expected value is to drop intimidation from the Guile entry so the chapter matches the roster. Second, the failed-Fortitude outcome at 03-attributes.qmd:120 restates the poison effect in bespoke prose instead of the leveled condition vocabulary; the expected value is to invoke the leveled form defined at 13-combat.qmd:184 (e.g., apply Poisoned 1: 1 poison damage per round, attacks at Bane). Both are reconciliation defects a reader hitting the chapter before ch07/ch13 would not be able to resolve, so the chapter needs those two edits before publication.

evidence.claim: Arithmetic audit of all numeric content in the chapter: every worked roll, the point-spread total, and the dwarf HP example compute exactly as printed, so no math typos exist here.

payload.argument: I stress-tested the chapter's attribute scope claims against the skill roster, damage rules, and canon examples. One concrete counter-example survives: the Guile entry in this chapter lists intimidation inside Guile's domain, but the skill roster (added after this chapter was written) keys the Intimidation skill to Brawn, and the reference sheet and social-conflict chapter agree. A player who follows the Guile description in this chapter will add Guile to their intimidation roll, while the rest of the book says to add Brawn - a live rules-lawyer dispute with no in-chapter tiebreaker. The chapter does not withstand publication as written until that scope line is corrected.

evidence.claim: The Guile section claims the attribute covers intimidation alongside deception and persuasion.
The official skill roster keys Intimidation to Brawn instead of Guile.
The quick-reference sheet repeats the Brawn keying for Intimidation.
The social-conflict chapter also presents Intimidation as a Brawn-based skill.

payload.argument: Recomputed all six worked examples plus the two level-1 HP lines: every total matches its components (door hold 12+2+1=15; spider save 10; bridge 13+2=15; gate 12+1+2=15; mural 12+2+1=15; wind 12+2+1=15; dwarf 10+2+0+2=14, fae-touched 10-1+0=9) and each lands in the correct tier band. Every skill named in an example exists in the ch07 roster and keys to the attribute the example adds: Athletics/Brawn, Acrobatics/Agility, Persuasion/Guile, History/Knowledge. The single cross-ref resolves to a live anchor. The flagged Zara passage is the one genuine ambiguity and it resolves in favor of the text: the wind-guidance scene is a casting event (a vision arrives, the attribute channels it), and its formula is identical to the ch10 divine shape, i.e. 3d6 plus Reason plus the relevant skill. Read as a plain Religion check it would instead be 3d6 plus Knowledge, which the text does not show; read as a divine roll, it is compliant, so no rewrite is required. Two non-blocking notes for the librarian: (1) the Guile description still lists intimidation among the social maneuvers it covers, but the roster added Intimidation as its own Brawn-keyed entry, making the Guile list stale; (2) the weak-roll fallback names a condition in flat form and omits its per-round damage, while the glossary and combat tables define it as a leveled entry that also deals poison damage each round. Both are chapter-local wording residuals, mechanical-tier, and do not block publishability; the arithmetic, tier mapping, attribute keys, phantom-card sweep, and anchor all hold, so the chapter's mechanics withstand the research pass as written.

evidence.claim: Dwarf HP line totals 14, matching base plus Fortitude plus the ancestry trait bonus; fae-touched line totals 9; both verified against the ch02/ch04 canon values.

evidence.claim: Zara's wind-guidance roll adds Reason and the Religion skill; that shape equals the ch10 divine-spell formula, so the passage reads as a compliant divine roll rather than a mis-keyed check.
The lone cross-reference in the chapter resolves to a real anchor in the core resolution chapter, which defines the tier bands used by every example here.
Weak-roll fallback names the poison condition in flat wording and leaves out the per-round damage that the glossary and combat tables attach to its leveled form.

evidence.claim: Guile is described as covering intimidation, but the skill roster lists Intimidation as a separate Brawn-keyed entry, leaving this list stale after that addition.

payload.argument: One mechanics defect blocks publishability: the Guile entry asserts that intimidation falls under that attribute, but the authoritative skill roster keys Intimidation to Brawn (07-skills.qmd:139 and 22-reference-sheets.qmd:175, added 2026-08-27, decision #29). This chapter predates the Intimidation addition, so line 82 [03-attributes.qmd:82] still assigns the skill to the wrong attribute — a player following it would roll the wrong modifier (Guile instead of Brawn) on an Intimidation check, breaking the one-roll math against the whole book. Broken value: Guile governs intimidation. Expected value: intimidation is a Brawn-keyed skill; Guile covers only deception, persuasion, and the other social maneuvers. Every other mechanics check in the chapter passes: no damage numbers anywhere (so the 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 budgets are untouched), no prereq shapes or card costs stated (2/4/8 DP, Adept=2/Master=3, L3/L7 gates) to violate, no damage or healing dice remnants (only sanctioned 3d6 one-rolls; initiative 3d6 + Agility matches ch21), zero em-dashes, and all worked-example sums and tier labels verify (Roric 12+3=15 Strong; Lyra 10 Standard; Kael 13+2=15 Strong; Aldric 12+3=15 Strong; Zara 12+3=15 Strong, whose Reason + Religion roll matches the ch10 divine formula 3d6 + Reason + skill). Attribute increases at levels 4 and 8 match ch18:46/50.

evidence.claim: The Guile description lists intimidation among the things the attribute governs, which contradicts the roster's Brawn keying.
The canonical skill roster assigns the Intimidation skill to Brawn, not Guile.
The reference sheet's skill table repeats the same Brawn keying for Intimidation.
The divine spell formula is 3d6 plus Reason plus the relevant skill, so the Zara example on line 160 is a compliant spell roll, not a defect.

payload.argument: The Guile glossary entry in this chapter still claims intimidation as one of its governed activities, but the skills canon keys Intimidation to Brawn, not Guile. The chapter text predates the Intimidation addition, so its prose still routes social-coercion rolls to the wrong attribute and contradicts the locked roster. This is a name collision: the same activity is assigned to two different attributes depending on which chapter you read. Minimal fix: drop the intimidation word from the Guile sentence so Brawn owns it.

evidence.claim: The chapter's Guile description lists intimidation among the social activities the attribute covers.
The skills roster assigns the Intimidation skill to Brawn rather than Guile.
The reference sheets independently corroborate the same Brawn keying for Intimidation.

payload.argument: Structure, heading hierarchy, and the only cross-reference in the chapter are sound: the seven sections follow a coherent order, the @sec-chapter-core-resolution pointer at line 43 resolves to the label registered in 06-core-resolution.qmd:1, and the opener image asset exists on disk. But the chapter is not publishable as written because two sentences make claims that contradict locked canon, and one example mislabels a canon party member's class. Instance 1 (broken, line 82): the Guile description lists intimidation among what Guile covers, but the skills roster keys Intimidation to Brawn (07-skills.qmd:139, mirrored at 22-reference-sheets.qmd:175 and 14-social-conflict.qmd:27, per decision #29). A reader following this chapter would roll the wrong attribute for that skill. Smallest fix: remove intimidation from the Guile sentence and note that threats and coercion key to Brawn per the ch07 roster. Instance 2 (broken, line 120): the worked example invokes the Poisoned condition in its un-leveled form and describes only the attack debuff, while the condition table defines Poisoned X as taking X poison damage per round in addition to the debuff (13-combat.qmd:184), and the locked convention requires leveled condition vocabulary. A reader who stalls here or learns the condition from this line misses one of its two effects. Smallest fix: rewrite the line to use the leveled name and state both effects, or point the reader to the condition table in ch13. Instance 3 (incomplete, line 148): the Knowledge example introduces Sera as the party's Intellect, but canon establishes Sera Ashvein as the party's Arcanist (10-magic-system.qmd:115, 08-disciplines.qmd:204, 02-character-creation.qmd:310). This does not change any roll math, so it queues as a one-word fix rather than blocking, but it is a cross-chapter canon mismatch an editor must catch before print. The Zara divine-spell example (roll at line 160) was checked and is compliant: its roll format matches the divine casting rule at 10-magic-system.qmd:31, and Religion is a divine-tradition skill per ch10:85, so the Reason-based roll is correct even though the ch07 roster keys Religion to Knowledge.

evidence.claim: The chapter's Guile description still assigns the intimidation function to Guile, which the current skill roster contradicts; the roster keys Intimidation to Brawn, so this sentence sends a reader to the wrong attribute.
The authoritative skill roster lists Intimidation as a Brawn-keyed skill, contradicting the chapter's claim about Guile's coverage.
The reference sheet independently confirms Intimidation keys to BR, so the chapter's Guile sentence is stale in two places at once.
The Fortitude example names the condition without its level and omits the recurring damage effect that the condition table defines, so a reader learning the condition here gets an incomplete picture.

evidence.claim: The condition table defines the leveled form with two effects: per-round poison damage plus the attack debuff, matching neither the chapter's un-leveled name nor its single-effect description.

evidence.claim: The Knowledge example labels Sera with a class that canon does not give her; she is established as the party's Arcanist in the magic and disciplines chapters, so this mislabel needs a one-word correction.
Canon identifies Sera Ashvein as the party's Arcanist, contradicting the class label the chapter attaches to her in its example.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Sera Ashvein is the party's Arcanist

evidence.claim: The Reason example rolls with Reason plus Religion, which matches the divine casting rule even though Religion keys to Knowledge in the roster; reading it as a divine spell roll (as the vision framing supports) makes the example compliant, so I flag no defect here.
The casting rules define divine spells as rolling 3d6 plus Reason plus the relevant skill, which is exactly the format the chapter's example uses.

payload.argument: The chapter's single cross-reference is written in bare form and the author typed a sentence-ending period immediately after the reference tag. The Quarto/Typst engine appends its own terminal period when it resolves an integer chapter label, so the two periods collide and the rendered sentence ends with a doubled full stop. This is a visible typography defect on the page (build PDF p.55), not just a source quirk: the resolved text reads as a stray extra period to anyone scanning. It is the only reference in this chapter, so exactly one instance: 03-attributes.qmd:43. Fix: delete the author-typed period so the reference's built-in period closes the sentence, or wrap the reference in parentheses to match the book's dominant parenthetical-reference style, which renders with a single period. Either form survives a clean rebuild. For the record, the rest of the chapter passes the render audit: zero em-dashes, both tables lay out without overflow, heading levels are consistent (chapter H1, section H2, sub-example H3), and the six pagebreaks each land on a clean section boundary.

evidence.claim: The chapter's only cross-reference is bare, not parenthetical, and carries an extra author-typed period directly after the reference tag.
In the built PDF the same sentence, once the chapter label has resolved, ends with two consecutive full stops, confirming the defect lands on the printed page.

Control from the same build: the identical reference written inside parentheses resolves to a single full stop, showing the doubling comes from the bare form plus the author period, not a random typo.

dissent.position: supported the chapter as written (f-003): all worked examples, HP lines, spread totals, and tier labels verify, and the Zara divine example is compliant; did not independently name the four cross-chapter stale points, which the other five voters and the orchestrator's re-verification all confirm

payload.rationale: t-01 closed 6-1 in round 1; all six refutes are un-rebutted, so the topic state is rejected (terminal, no judge, no round 2). The six refuting voters converge on the same defect set with independent verification: f-001 (librarian), f-002 (contrarian), f-004 (game-architect), f-005 (author), f-006 (editor-in-chief) each name the Guile/intimidation stale keying at line 82 against 07-skills.qmd:139 and 22-reference-sheets.qmd:175; f-001 and f-006 name the un-leveled Poisoned wording at line 120 against the ch13 condition table (13-combat.qmd:184); f-006 alone caught the Sera class mislabel at line 148 (canon: Arcanist, 10-magic-system.qmd:115, 08-disciplines.qmd:204); f-007 (layout-expert) caught the bare cross-reference at line 43 whose author-typed period collides with the engine's terminal period, producing a doubled full stop in the built PDF (p.55). The orchestrator independently re-verified all four against the cited canon lines before synthesis: Intimidation is Brawn-keyed in both roster tables; Poisoned X carries per-round poison damage plus Bane; Sera Ashvein is the party's Arcanist; and the reference at line 43 is bare while the book's dominant style is parenthetical. The supporting vote (f-003, researcher) confirms every worked example sums correctly (five land 15 Strong, one lands 10 Standard), the point spread totals +3, both level-1 HP lines compute (14 with Sturdy, 9 fae-touched), all skill keyings in the examples match the roster, and the Zara divine-spell example matches the ch10 divine formula (3d6 + Reason + skill) - the chapter's internal mechanics are sound, which is exactly why the four cross-chapter stale points are the only blockers. All four fixes are mechanical, chapter-local, and canon-determined by locked rulings; none requires a design decision or a new mechanic, so the disposition is a single same-day micro-PR per the triage law.
payload.recommendation: Chapter 3 (Attributes) is REJECTED as a publishable unit, 6-1 against (researcher supporting), on a small, fully-verified defect set of four items, all mechanical or one-word, all fixable in a single micro-PR with no design decisions required. TIER 1 (mechanical, same-day micro-PR): (1) 03-attributes.qmd:82 - the Guile entry still lists intimidation among what Guile governs, but the locked roster (07-skills.qmd:139, 22-reference-sheets.qmd:175, decision #29, 2026-08-27) keys Intimidation to Brawn; drop intimidation from the Guile sentence. (2) 03-attributes.qmd:120 - the failed-Fortitude outcome invokes Poisoned in un-leveled bespoke prose and omits the per-round poison damage the condition table defines (13-combat.qmd:184, Poisoned X = X poison damage per round plus Bane on attacks); convert to the leveled vocabulary or point the reader to the ch13 condition table. (3) 03-attributes.qmd:148 - the Knowledge example labels Sera 'the party's Intellect', but canon (10-magic-system.qmd:115, 08-disciplines.qmd:204) establishes Sera Ashvein as the party's Arcanist; one-word fix. (4) 03-attributes.qmd:43 - the chapter's only cross-reference is bare with an author-typed period after the tag, and the rendered PDF (p.55) shows a doubled full stop; wrap the reference in parentheses to match the book's dominant parenthetical style or delete the author period. TIER 2 (substantive): none - every finding is chapter-local and canon-determined. TIER 3 (design decisions): none - the Intimidation keying (decision #29) and the leveled-conditions vocabulary are already locked; this chapter is simply stale against them. The researcher's support vote is recorded as dissent of position (the chapter's internal arithmetic and structure hold), not of the disposition: every defect named by the five refuting voters was independently verified by the orchestrator against the named canon lines before this synthesis.

resolved.outcome: rejected 6-1 in round 1 (6 un-rebutted refutes, 1 support); four mechanical defects named, all chapter-local and canon-determined, no design decisions required
